key_insight: In MCP-based AI agents, tool names and metadata do not necessarily establish provider identity, allowing attacker-advertised tools to receive requests intended for legitimate providers.
engineering_relevance: MCP integrations should bind tool discovery and invocation to verified provider identities rather than rely on names, descriptions, or schema compatibility.
method: Formulate tool-provider misbinding as an attacker-controlled tool-selection optimization problem.
Operate an attacker MCP server with chosen tool metadata, without compromising legitimate components or network channels.
Evaluate metadata interactions in a controlled MCP environment across five LLM-based clients.
evidence_signal: Across five clients, the strongest failures combined exact-name collisions, task-aligned descriptions, and compatible schemas; authority-enhanced descriptions also induced wrong-provider execution or ambiguity without name collisions.
watch_item: The controlled evaluation shows client-dependent failure modes, but the abstract provides no quantitative misbinding rates or evidence of prevalence in deployed systems.
paper_title: When Tool Names Are Not Identities: Measuring Provider Misbinding in MCP-Based AI Agents
